This suggests that 1,2-Dihydroxybenzene may exert its effects through different mechanisms, potentially modulating the activity of multiple enzymes before reaching Cyanovirin-N. The integration of these pathways implies that 1,2-Dihydroxybenzene could act as a modulator of metabolic processes, influencing enzyme activity and thereby affecting Cyanovirin-N's function. The evidence supports a mechanistic link, but further investigation is needed to determine the precise role of 1,2-Dihydroxybenzene in the regulation of Cyanovirin-N.
